summary: Nora now records, for each turn, whether what she said was actually supported by what she had — and when it was not, which claims had no source behind them. It is written once per turn and never revised.
details: This is about SOURCING, not about being right or being helpful. A short unhelpful reply that claimed nothing counts as grounded; a fluent useful one that invented a detail does not. A turn where she deliberately said nothing is grounded, because she asserted nothing.

It is deliberately kept apart from the running position, which is rewritten every turn. A per-turn judgement stored on a row that gets overwritten has a lifetime of one turn — that was a real bug in an earlier draft, and the separation is what prevents it.

A judgement that cannot be saved never costs the position. The position is what she reads on her next turn; the judgement is for a later rebuild, so it is written afterwards and its failure is counted on its own.
limitations: Nothing reads these rows yet. The pass that would rebuild a drifted position from them is not built, so for now this accumulates a record and changes nothing she does.
The judgement is the model's own about the turn it just reviewed, not an independent check. It is evidence to look at, not a verdict to trust.
